Reviewed the complete supplied source/brief, complete draft, and supplied quotation guidance. Resolved language: en_US. No translations occur. ## Source passages

S1: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”

S2: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”

S4: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks.”

S5: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

S6: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”

S7: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”

S8: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

S9: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

S10: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

S11: “Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”

S12: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided.”

S13 (brief): “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party.”

S14 (brief): “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”

1. Draft: title, “Elm Quay brings repair reports into one shared view.” Proposition: Elm Quay brings repair reports into a shared view in the described trial. Support ruling it out: S2, “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.” Supported intention, not a measured universal access outcome.

This states the note's attribution, not proof that software had no effect.

Smallest supported repair: replace “because telephone reports and emails had been stored separately” with a new sentence, “Previously, telephone reports and emails had been stored separately.” Preserve the September decision and the stated purpose elsewhere.

The figures preserve assignment rather than completion, medians and working-day units, the preceding eight-week comparison, workload qualification, and explicit nonattribution. Counts are not evaluated as high or low. The account maintains the customer as acting party and the supplier in third person. No invented scene, emotion, personal experience, comparative supplier ranking, cost benefit, or satisfaction outcome occurs.
